data.title: Nalongo Namubiru's Story
data.luganda_text: Nze Nalongo Namubiru. Nazaalibwa mu Masaka mu mwaka gwa 1948. Taata wange yali ayitibwa Kizito, era yali mulimi wa mmwanyi. Maama wange Nakato yatusomesanga engero buli kiro ku kyoto. Bwe nnali muwala muto twagenda e Kampala okulaba Kabaka. Taata yatugamba nti, "Agali awamu ge galuma enyama." Mu biseera bya Amin twadduka ne tugenda ewa jjajja e Mpigi. Eyo gye nnasisinkana bba wange Ssemakula.
data.english_text: I am Nalongo Namubiru. I was born in Masaka in 1948. My father was called Kizito, and he was a coffee farmer. My mother Nakato used to teach us folk tales every night by the fireplace. When I was a young girl, we went to Kampala to see the Kabaka. Father told us, "Teeth that are together are the ones that bite the meat." During Amin's time we fled and went to my grandparent's home in Mpigi. That is where I met my husband Ssemakula.
